title: High-protein foods that aren't meat

seo.title: High-protein foods that aren't meat
seo.meta_description: Eggs, dairy, fish, soy foods, legumes, seitan, nuts and seeds can all provide protein without meat. Compare realistic servings, not just 100-gram rankings.
seo.search_intent: Find substantial protein sources that do not require meat and compare them in realistic portions.

excerpt: You can get a substantial amount of protein without meat. Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, eggs, fish, tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame and legumes can all contribute meaningfully; the useful comparison is how much protein a normal serving supplies, not which food looks most concentrated per 100 grams.
content_html:
Removing meat does not leave a protein vacuum. The bigger question is what else you eat and in what quantity. A tablespoon of peanut butter technically contains protein, but it is not equivalent to a cup of Greek yogurt or a serving of tempeh.

The following comparison uses realistic portions so foods are judged in the way they are actually eaten.

FoodTypical servingProtein
Seitan100 gabout 24–25 g
Greek yogurt, plain200 gabout 18–20 g
Cottage cheese1 cup / ~200 gabout 22–26 g
Tempeh100 gabout 19–20 g
Firm tofu150 gabout 18–25 g
Edamame1 cup cookedabout 17–18 g
Lentils1 cup cookedabout 18 g
Eggs2 largeabout 12–13 g
Almonds1 ozabout 6 g

The table shows why serving size matters. Nuts are protein-containing foods, but a one-ounce serving adds about 6 g; lentils, tofu or dairy can provide three or four times as much in a normal meal-sized portion.

Plant foods can be major protein sources, not just side dishes

Soy foods, seitan and legumes work best when they are treated as the protein anchor of the meal. A bowl built around 1 cup of lentils can provide roughly 18 g of protein before bread, grains or toppings are counted. A 150 g serving of firm tofu can reach around 20 g or more, depending on the product.

Eggs and dairy make the target easier for vegetarians

Two eggs provide about 12–13 g, while strained yogurt and cottage cheese can reach roughly 20–25 g per substantial serving. That makes them useful for breakfast or snacks when the rest of the meal is not especially protein-rich.

Fish is not meat, but it changes the dietary pattern

If the goal is literally to avoid meat rather than follow a vegetarian diet, fish is another highly concentrated source: many cooked fish provide roughly 20–30 g protein per 100 g. A pescatarian pattern therefore has different options from a vegetarian or vegan one.

The practical rule

Choose one clearly substantial protein source at each main meal, then let grains, vegetables, nuts and seeds add to it. The most useful question is not whether a food contains protein, but whether the portion you actually eat contributes 5 g, 15 g or 25 g.

faq.question: What are the highest-protein foods without meat?
faq.answer: Seitan, strained dairy, tempeh, firm tofu, edamame and legumes are among the most useful options by realistic serving. Eggs and fish also qualify if they fit the dietary pattern.

faq.question: Are nuts a main protein source?
faq.answer: They contribute protein, but a 1-ounce serving of almonds provides only about 6 g, so nuts usually complement rather than replace a meal-sized protein source.
